issue_context.title: [KMSv2] Use status key ID to determine staleness of encrypted data
issue_context.body:
Today you need multiple encryption providers to communicate to the API server if data stored in etcd is stale (i.e. the KMS v1beta1 API has no way to communicate staleness).  The KMS v2 API includes a key ID in the status API to allow for such a check to be performed.  We need to wire the knowledge of the current key ID into the envelope encryption code.

xref: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/111126#discussion_r934870019

/assign
/milestone v1.26
/sig auth
/triage accepted

review_comments:
AFAIK, errors don't have log severity

```suggestion
					klog.ErrorS(err, "kms plugin failed health check probe", "name", kmsName)
```
My understanding is that this will emit an error log but only if log level is at least 2.
I believe you need to initialize this with an empty string in `kmsPrefixTransformer` to avoid `nil` pointer panics.
We need to update `isKMSv2ProviderHealthy` to use `validateKeyID`.

```suggestion
		// make sure that the plugin's key ID is reasonably up-to-date
		go wait.PollImmediateUntilWithContext(
```

I would add some basic unit tests to exercise the key ID getter.

More importantly, I would like to see an integration test that performs a no-op update on a single item and confirms that when the key IDs are the same the RV does not change, and when key ID changes the RV changes (but only once).  You will need to do some form of polling with the `wait` package.
If there is no error, do we still need to poll? If not this would go into `if err != nil` loop and we would just return true here?
This is meant to run forever: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/114544#discussion_r1065151069
At the end of this test, I think we should disable the plugin, confirm that creating a _new_ secret fails, but that a no-op update does not fail.

@liggitt this PR makes the API server coast (forever) on the last successful key ID it got from the plugin.  Thus staleness checks for read calls will not fail if the plugin is down transiently.  At a high level I believe we have three choices here:

1. Coast on the last key ID, no error, staleness based on last observed key ID
2. Error and fail the read request (would partially defeat the purpose of having a cache since we would no longer tolerate plugin downtime)
3. Mark the read request as `stale=true` - for no-op updates this would cause a write (which would presumably fail since the plugin is down)

What do you think is the best approach here?
Maybe another option is to make `stale` a `*bool` to try and express the "I do not know" state?

it's hard to imagine life being better for a cluster admin if we make the cluster start failing reads ... I wouldn't do that.

failing no-op writes doesn't seem useful to me either... it pushes errors to users unlikely to be able to do anything about them

I think I would expect to coast, and for an error here to increment a metric to make it clear something is not working as expected (either transiently or persistently)
Opened https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/115188 to add metrics as a follow up.
Trying to think if there is a way to have an integration test that proves that this loop is running. 🤔
Check the error and return early.
